Issued at 1105 PM CST Mon Nov 2 2026

Earlier this evening an upper level trough was located over 
western Kansas. Under this upper level trough a strong cold 
front was crossing southwest Kansas with surface observations 
already reporting wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph reported behind 
this front at of 04z. This cold front will continue to cross all
of southwest Kansas by early Tuesday morning as this upper 
level trough moves slowly east/northeast across Kansas. The 
strong gusty winds behind this front will continue through 
Tuesday and usher in some colder air into the area which will 
result in afternoon temperatures Tuesday afternoon being around 
15 degrees cooler compared to the highs that occurred across 
southwest Kansas on earlier today (Monday). Given these 
temperatures and strong gusty winds expected through the day it 
will feel colder than this Tuesday afternoon. Afternoon wind 
chills in the 40s/lower 50s will be possible for many locations 
west or north of Dodge City. The ongoing convection across 
portions of southwest Kansas early this morning from the wrap 
around moisture and enhanced lift near the 500mb deformation 
zone just W/NW of the upper trough will taper off from southwest
to northeast by noon.

Very windy conditions late tonight and Tuesday with wind gusts 
of 45 to 55 mph possible through at least noon Tuesday. An upper
level trough crossing western Kansas will deepen a surface low 
over Central Kansas overnight and early Tuesday. This will 
result in tight surface pressure gradient over southwest Kansas.
This combined with forecast 850mb north northwest winds of 45 
to 50 knots indicated the potential for wind gusts to be 
stronger than what the latest NBM guidance suggest, at least 
through 18z Tuesday. BUFR soundings momentum transfer and even 
the REFS 10m wind gusts both are in agreement with the potential
stronger winds/wind gusts. Based on this combined with the 04z 
surface observations behind this cold front it appears the 
stronger winds will be more reasonable. Have therefore favored 
the stronger 75th percentile of the NBM for winds over the next 
24-36 hours. 

Temperatures falling back into the 30 to 35 degree range early 
Wednesday morning west and north of the Dodge City area. Early 
Tuesday night the gusty northwest winds which ushered in the 
cold air into southwest Kansas Monday night and Tuesday will 
decrease to less than 10 mph as the surface pressure gradient 
weakens across southwest Kansas. Clear skies and light winds 
Tuesday night will create a favorable environment for 
temperatures to easily fall back well into the 30s by early 
Wednesday morning with frost or even a few locations waking up 
to temperatures around 32, mainly west and north of the Dodge 
City area.

Seasonal Temperatures late week with a 40-70% chance for light 
rain Wednesday night. As our Monday storm system moves east of 
the area Tuesday and progressive, weaker, upper level trough 
will take aim on western Kansas mid week. Ensembles were in good
agreement with weak forcing and limited moisture will be 
present ahead of this next system as the upper wave quickly 
crossing western Kansas Wednesday night. As a result the
ensemble clusters have only a 20-40% chance for 24 hour 
rainfall totals ending at 6pm Thursday to be greater than 0.25 
inches. A surface boundary/weak cold front will briefly move 
into southwest Kansas following this upper trough but then 
quickly lift back north. This will keep temperatures in the 
50s/lower 60s Wednesday and Thursday and then warm back into the
mid 60s by Friday/Saturday as an upper level ridge exits the 
Rockies and moves out into the plains. These temperatures late 
week are near the seasonal normals for this time of year.
